Q: How to escape starting new line from amidi dump to pass it in a while read loop in bash A:

A simplistic solution, but a quick literal check might be all you need.

while read -r hex; do [[ -z "$hex" ]] && continue

That should ignore blank lines.

ABSTRACT

This study investigates the adaptation and implementation of Lean Manufacturing principles to enhance production efficiency in the Bus Assembly Line of the Bishoftu Motor Vehicles Engineering Industry (BMEVI) within the Ethiopian context. Employing a mixed-methods case study design, the research integrates quantitative performance measurements with qualitative insights from 62 employee surveys and 8 managerial interviews, supplemented by direct observation and time studies. The findings reveal pervasive operational inefficiencies across all eight Lean wastes, with waiting time (due to equipment breakdowns) and inventory waste (from overproduction) being particularly prominent. Estimated Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) falls below 60%, significantly below world-class benchmarks. While organizational readiness shows positive indicators in workforce willingness, critical gaps exist in management's deep understanding of Lean philosophy and a compliance-based culture resistant to foundational practices like 5S. The study proposes a contextualized three-phase Lean implementation framework prioritizing foundational stability through 5S, basic Total Productive Maintenance, and standardized work before introducing flow and pull systems. Key recommendations include strategic buffer inventories to address volatile supply chains, comprehensive Lean education for management, and alignment of performance metrics with value stream efficiency. This research contributes to the emerging literature on Lean adaptation in developing economies, demonstrating that successful implementation requires a "stability-first, context-aware" approach that accommodates infrastructural and cultural realities while maintaining core Lean principles.

Keywords: Lean Manufacturing, Production Efficiency, Waste Elimination, Automotive Industry, Ethiopian Context, Operational Performance, Value Stream Mapping, 5S, Total Productive Maintenance, Developing Economies.

Q: Expo Application Services (EAS) Build keeps failing with a "spawn git ENOENT" error A:

I fixed the issue myself, but if anyone happens to stumble across this in a future, it apparently happened after installing some other unrelated tools on my computer which included their own version of git.exe, causing trouble since eas used the wrong git. It was fixed after uninstalling that version of git and keeping only the one in C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe.

Q: How to correctly symbolicate PLCrashReporter crash reports using dSYM files? A:

What you're seeing is expected behavior.

plcrashutil convert does not symbolicate, it only converts the binary PLCrashReporter format into an Apple-style .crash text file. Symbolication is always a separate, post-processing step that requires matching dSYM files.

The reliable workflow is a two-step process, first you need to convert the uploaded crash report into a readable crash log:

plcrashutil convert --format=ios crash.plcrash > crash.raw.crash

At this stage the log is valid but unsymbolicated. Although plcrashutil itself has no --dsym option and does not perform symbolication, the dSYM files are provided explicitly in the next step using Apple's symblocation tools.

xcrun crashlog \
  --symbolicate \
  --dsym /path/to/dSYMs \
  crash.raw.crash

If your app includes embedded frameworks, pass a directory containing all relevant dSYMs instead of a single file; this approach should work for device builds, ad-hoc builds, TestFlight, etc.. as long as the UUIDs in the crash log match those in the dSYMs. Simulaator crashes may already appear symbolicated due to host-side symbols but real devices always require correct dSYMs:

symbolicatecrash crash.raw.crash /path/to/dSYMs/

There's no supported way to symbolicate at runtime or to "inject" symbols into a PLCrashReporter report; symbolication is intentionally a post-processing step based on UUID matching, mirroring Apple's own crash pipeline.

Best practice setup outside of their-party services is to archive dSYMs per app version, convert incoming .plcrash files server-side, symbolicate them using explicit dSYM paths, and retain both raw and symbolicated logs for analysis.

Q: What will be next time? A:

How can we survive in this AI-dominated world?

What exactly threatens your survival?

You've indicated that:

  • New tools exist ("I know that AI coding tools are completely transforming the software industry")
  • You are successfully using those tools ("I use a tool called Cursor to build full-stack apps very quickly")
  • You expect those tools will continue to improve ("it will only become more powerful in the future")

If your current experience and outlook on the subject are objectively good and positive things, what actual problem are you trying to solve?

Don't let the hype coming from the screens around you cause you to panic. That hype is just trying to sell you something.
